Day 23 – Vectorised Landmask Raster

Date: 2026-02-07
Goal: Improve landmask raster performance by vectorising grid evaluation.

🗺️ Context: With the landmask being successfully rendered without colour spillage into the oceans, via rasters, 
            the next step is to optimise; cut runtime. The previous approach, while successful, was ~O(N_points x N_polygons).
	    At 1 deg resolution, 181 x 365 = 65,000 grid points
	                                   * hundreds of polygons
                                           * slider interaction
            ...which is not scalable.

Why vectorise: 
   	•	Speed - instead of loops, let NumPy operate on entire arrays in C
	•	Clean architecture - separate grid generation from polygon membership logic from mask accumulation
	•	Scalable - to numba, multiprocessing, spatial indexing

✅ Achievements
	•	Replaced nested (lat, lon) loops with flattened meshgrid approach.
	•	Flattened grid into 1D arrays for single-pass evaluation.
	•	Rasterised using one loop over flattened points instead of double loop (over lat, over lon).

🔍 Insights
	•	Eliminating nested loops simplifies control flow and improves readability.
	•	Flattened raster structure makes future optimisations (bounding boxes, masking, parallelisation) easier.
	•	Performance bottleneck is now strictly polygon membership testing.

🚧 Next steps
	•	Introduce polygon-level spherical bounding boxes to reduce unnecessary point tests.
	•	Explore spatial indexing or latitude band pre-bucketing.
	•	Benchmark 1.0° vs 0.5° resolution runtime.
